observations: Three photos show multiple dark blue laptops, all with the same design and branding.
The laptops are open and arranged in a fan-like display on a carpeted floor.
The keyboard has 'ELITEBOOK' printed on the lower left corner in photo 0 and photo 1.
The HP logo is visible on the lid in photo 2.
The laptops appear to be 2-in-1 convertible models with hinges allowing the screen to fold back.
A small blue sticker with 'Intel Core' is visible on the keyboard area in photo 0 and photo 1.
The screen is glossy and reflects the surroundings, including a camera or phone in photo 1.
No visible damage or wear is apparent in the photos, but close-up details of ports, screen, or internal components are missing.
Watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI RAYTK TECH' is overlaid on all photos.

claims.evidence: Photos show the laptops are in good condition, but there is no proof of origin (London) or grading (Grade A).
No warranty documentation, sticker, or proof is visible in the photos. Cannot verify remotely.

risks.risk: Laptop may have hidden physical damage or defects not visible in photos (e.g., screen burn-in, hinge wear, internal damage).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the screen, hinges, ports, and underside of the laptop.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially defective or with reduced value due to hidden damage.

risks.risk: Battery health or performance may be degraded, especially if used and imported from London.
risks.proof: Video or photo showing battery health report or usage time on battery.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as if battery is not fully functional or degraded.

risks.risk: Laptop may not be genuine or may have been refurbished without proper documentation.
risks.proof: Serial number photo and verification via HP website or official channel.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially counterfeit or unverified refurbished unit.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the serial number on the bottom of the laptop.
Photo or video showing the screen and hinge in full motion and under different lighting.
Photo of the battery health report or power settings screen.
Proof of warranty (if any) or documentation of origin (London).
response.reason: The laptops are identifiable as HP EliteBook models, but critical claims like 'Grade A', 'London used', and 'warranty' cannot be verified from the photos. Hidden risks such as battery health, screen condition, and authenticity require additional proof before pricing can be determined accurately.
